To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a failover mechanism for distributed SDN Controllers that is based on a pre-partition strategy.

(1) we have proposed two strategies for failover in distributed SDN controllers, (2) we have built a prototype with Floodlight distributed controllers to evaluate these two strategies, (3) we have shown that the pre-partition approach enables a quick failover of orphan OpenFlow switch, (4) we have also shown that the pre partition approach introduces a very low additional control traffic.

we propose two strategies for failover in distributed SDN controllers, one that is greedy and another that partitions the network in advance, and that we evaluate these strategies in a prototype with Floodlight controllers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How to build a distributed SDN controller that provides high availability? (2) What are the trade-offs between consistency and availability?
the design, analysis, and implementation of distributed SDN controllers, and in particular with their failover mechanisms.
the design, implementation, and evaluation of distributed SDN controllers for the Internet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed failover mechanism can be applied in any distributed controller architecture.
the proposed failover strategies are effective for distributed SDN architectures and the pre-partitioned strategy is more efficient in terms of failover time.

the failover time of the greedy strategy is proportional to the amount of orphaned switches and that the pre-partitioned approach enables to quickly react in less than 100ms with a very small additional overhead.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a failover strategy for distributed SDN controller architectures, which can reduce the time to react to the failure of a controller.
the distributed SDN controllers can provide high resilience against controller failures, but at the cost of some additional latency.
we proposed a distributed SDN controller architecture and a failover mechanism to ensure the resilience of the SDN controller.
The main takeaway from our work is that
distributed SDN controllers are a viable solution to improve the resilience of SDN networks.
a failover mechanism is needed to guarantee the availability of the network and that the pre-partition approach is the most suitable to address this issue.
distributed SDN controllers are not resilient by design, and that a careful failover design is needed to achieve a resilient SDN architecture.
